candidates.problem: Windows Task Scheduler state for long-running autonomous software (JARVIS Supervisor continuity, worker restarts) is managed by hand-written schtasks subprocess calls and hand-copied XML. Recorded consequences: an S3 byte-fidelity incident (CRLF/UTF-16 mismatch between declared and archived task XML), recurring lane blockers on shared scheduler staging tests, and test-residue tasks left on the host.
candidates.target_user: Autonomous agent runtimes and Windows automation engineers managing scheduled tasks as reviewable state
candidates.proposed_artifact: taskward - zero-dependency Python CLI/library: scoped export (byte-exact XML + SHA-256), validate, plan (declared-vs-live diff gate with exit codes), idempotent apply restricted to a dedicated folder scope
candidates.mvp_boundary: Four subcommands (export/validate/plan/apply) operating only under a lab scope folder \JarvisLab\; live host integration proven end-to-end non-elevated; no GUI, no remote hosts, no credential storage
kill_criteria: If non-elevated task CRUD under a user-writable folder proves impossible on this host
If PowerShell JSON bridging cannot be made locale/version-stable
If drift comparison produces >20% false diffs on unchanged tasks
candidates.success_metric: Fresh verifier passes all acceptance criteria incl. full create->drift->repair->delete cycle on the real host with Critical=0
